title: Write your own style flattener
prompt:
React Native merges a `style` prop the same way every time: arrays are read left to right, later keys win, falsy entries are skipped, and arrays can nest. Implement `flattenStyle(style)` so it follows those rules and returns **one new plain object**.

- An object returns a copy of itself.
- A falsy value (`false`, `null`, `undefined`) or an empty array returns `{}`.
- It must never mutate the style objects you pass in.

The starter is close but has three bugs. Find them.
hints: `Object.assign(style[0], …)` writes into the first object. What happens to a shared `styles.card` the next time it's used?
Handle the simple cases first: falsy input returns `{}`, and a non-array object returns `{ ...style }`.
For arrays, start from `const result = {}` and `Object.assign(result, flattenStyle(entry))` for each entry; the recursive call takes care of nesting and falsy entries.
explanation: The solution is recursive: every entry is flattened on its own, which handles nested arrays and falsy values with the same two base cases, and is merged into a fresh object so the caller's styles are never touched. Mutating `style[0]` is the dangerous bug: `styles.card` is shared by every card, so one favorite card would quietly change all of them. This is the same contract as `StyleSheet.flatten`, and knowing it lets you predict exactly what any style array will render.

checks.single-object: A single object comes back with the same keys
checks.skips-falsy: false, null and undefined entries are skipped
checks.nested-arrays: Nested arrays are flattened in order
checks.no-mutation: Input style objects are never modified
checks.falsy-input: Falsy input and empty arrays return {}
